wire.headline: Energy Firm Cuts Jobs and Closes Plants as Profits Fall
sentences: Revenue rose 7% year on year to 4.26bn GBP for the quarter to 30 September.
Pre-tax profit declined by 12% to 310m GBP.
The company plans to cut 850 jobs, which represents about 6% of the workforce.
Two gas plants will close by March 2027, with one located in Wales and the other in Kent.
CEO Marian Holt stated that cost pressure was sharper than expected.
Ofgem has opened an investigation into the company's billing system.
The dividend was held at 12.4p a share.

ND.headline: Energy Firm Reports Profit Drop and Plans Job Cuts

sentences.text: The company reported a pre-tax profit of 310m GBP, representing a 12% decrease.
The firm intends to cut 850 jobs, which accounts for about 6% of its workforce.
Negotiations with unions are scheduled to begin on 4 November.
The union Unite plans to ballot its members on taking industrial action.
An analyst from Kestrel Securities stated that the job cuts will save 90m GBP a year.
Kestrel Securities lowered its price target from 290p to 240p.
Shares closed at 268p, marking a drop of 11p.
The company declared that there will be no compulsory redundancies before January 2027.
Since 2024, 1,200 staff have left the company under a voluntary scheme.
The Kent plant employs 410 staff and the local supply chain is exposed.
The MP for Deeside has requested an urgent meeting with the company.
A customer group recorded 3,400 billing complaints in six months.
Ofgem fined the company 1.8m GBP in 2023 over billing issues.
Ofgem is expected to report preliminary findings by end of 2026.
This story is reported by Western Mail.
